For a binary outcome $Y_i \sim \Bernoulli(\prob_i)$
with $\logit(\prob_i) = \dprod{\vxi}{\vcoef}$,
the [logistic regression](https://morrison-lab.github.io/rme/chapters/logistic-regression.html) model,
a Bayesian analysis places a prior on the coefficient vector $\vcoef$
and samples the posterior $\p(\vcoef \mid \vy)$ by MCMC
[@dobson4e, Chapter 14, p. 318].
Each $\coef{x_j}$ is summarized by the mean and quantiles of its draws.
No large-sample Gaussian approximation is needed:
a credible interval is read directly from the posterior quantiles,
and the posterior of an odds ratio $e^{\coef{x_j}}$,
or of any other function of $\vcoef$,
is obtained by transforming the draws.
